note: Filled from local runs on the branch feat/app-platform-retention (cut from integration/app-platform at f3812948). Every limit is exercised by advancing the nowMS argument of the sweep; no elapsed real time and no CI run is cited. PostgreSQL 18.6 on a throwaway local database.

implemented.review_plan_validity: one constant, platformReviewPlanValidityMS (15 minutes), in the 12 expiry sites and the overflow guards beside them; unconsumed plans removed 24 hours after expiry when nothing references them
implemented.operations: app_platform_retention_operation_days, default 90, 90-365; completed operations deleted with effects and plan under the pin rule of doc 172 section 3
implemented.tasks: terminal tasks older than 30 days, or beyond 10000 unreduced rows per installation, reduced to tombstones (payload empty, result NULL, attempts deleted; occurrence_id, payload_sha256, handler kept); tombstones deleted after the operations period
implemented.runner_logs: json-file max-size 5m, max-file 2 (10 MiB per container); validContainerPlan refuses other options
implemented.recovery_sets: app_platform_retention_recovery_sets, default 2, 1-2, stored and clamped; sets beyond the latest N selected and reported only
implemented.scheduling: platformRetentionTick from cleanupTick; hourly when idle, minute cadence while a batch bound was hit; batches of 500 per class; one audit_log row per sweep (action app_platform.retention_sweep, actor system); nothing during the restore pause; fails closed on an unreadable pause marker
implemented.ui: AppPlatformRetentionCard in the storage page, GET and PUT /api/admin/app-platform/retention behind the cleanup permission

tests.drivers: each sweep test runs on SQLite and, with TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, on PostgreSQL; both were run and passed
tests.mutation_checks: removing the unresolved-effect pin, the recovery-chain pin, the capability-grant pin, the open-image pin or replacing the task reduction with a delete each failed a named test

assertions: only eligible rows are deleted, for plans, operations with effects and plans, tasks and tombstones
every pinned row is kept, with one fixture per pin and per reader group
an idempotency key inside the period still returns the original operation; past the period it resolves to no operation
a replayed occurrence of a swept task is deduplicated, a different payload hash conflicts, and after the tombstone is removed the occurrence is a new request
the per-installation cap (an injected 3) reduces only the oldest surplus; the default cap is 10000
one audit row per sweep with counts per class in detail
no work, no audit row, while the Portal is in the restore pause
retained namespaces, their recovery sets, the installation and the holding operation are unchanged 400 days later
the clamp on read and the refusal on save of both adjustable values
known_limits: recovery sets beyond the latest N are selected and reported, not removed: the runner has no command that deletes one checkpoint (delete-data removes a whole namespace), and marking a set deleted without its archive would leak runner disk
the 7-day runner log age is not enforceable by Docker's json-file driver; the 10 MiB size bound applies and logs go away with the container
the RUN-08 log flood evidence was measured at the previous 1 MiB policy and was not repeated at 5 MiB
no run covers the real retention periods or a production-size database; the sweep scans image-kind effects and recovery sets in full each time
an operation that is pinned (checkpoint operations through the recovery set foreign key, operations that loaded an image still on a runner) stays replayable past 90 days
the pin rule is derived from reading the readers of old operations, not proven exhaustive; the secret-binding plan reference has no fixture of its own
the sweep was not run against concurrent live installs
